strengths: Addresses a genuine and under-addressed problem in SNN-RL with clear problem motivation (Figure 1)
Solid theoretical foundation with principled derivation of confidence-weighted updates via Kalman filtering framework
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning multiple environments, neuron models, and RL algorithms with consistent improvements (up to 22.6%)
Thorough ablation studies and appropriate negative control (CaRe-BN on ANNs) strengthen claims
Practical design preserving inference procedure ensures zero deployment overhead
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured paper
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: confidence-adaptive update is straightforward Kalman filtering application; re-calibration is simple engineering

Significant theoretical gaps: Gaussian assumption (Eq. 1) questionable for discrete spike activations; approximations in Eqs. 10-11 lack rigorous justification; no empirical validation of approximation quality
Unsubstantiated core claims: energy efficiency and neuromorphic benefits claimed throughout but never measured; no power consumption analysis, latency measurements, or hardware deployment
Narrow experimental scope: only continuous control (MuJoCo); no discrete action spaces; all simulation-only (no neuromorphic hardware); relatively large timestep (5) with unclear scalability
Incomplete hyperparameter analysis: multiple hyperparameters (α, Tcal, M) introduced with minimal sensitivity analysis and no practitioner guidance
Missing diagnostic analysis: no visualization of confidence statistics evolution; no estimated vs. true statistics comparison; high variance in some results unexplained (e.g., Ant-v4: 5373±159)
Baseline fairness concerns: ANN baseline explicitly shallow (256 neurons, 2 layers)—not competitive; unclear if comparison methods optimized equally; BN baselines designed for supervised learning
Reproducibility gaps: code availability not mentioned; hyperparameter selection procedure underspecified; calibration batch selection details missing

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies and illustrates BN breakdown in online RL with non-stationary distributions, addressing a genuine gap in existing SNN-RL literature
Principled theoretical foundation: Theorem 1 provides rigorous MSE-optimal derivation of confidence-adaptive update with elegant Kalman filter connection

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple neuron models (LIF, CLIF), algorithms (DDPG, TD3), five benchmarks, comparisons with SOTA methods, and proper statistical reporting across 5 random seeds
Strong and consistent empirical results: 22.6% performance improvement, SNNs outperforming ANNs by 5.9%, and reduced variance (17-21% lower than ANN baselines) across diverse settings
Practical design: Maintains energy efficiency (unchanged inference), minimal computational overhead O(M/T_cal), seamless drop-in replacement for existing pipelines
Clear presentation: Well-organized structure, effective visualizations (especially Figure 1), and lucid writing make the contribution accessible
weaknesses: Incomplete theoretical analysis: Re-BN lacks theoretical justification, convergence analysis, or guidance for choosing critical hyperparameters (T_cal, M); Theorem 1 only covers Ca-BN component

Questionable core assumption: Gaussianity assumption (Assumption 1) is suspect for SNNs that produce sparse discrete outputs; lacks empirical validation and clarity on where/when activations are Gaussian

Problematic approximations: Eq. 10-11 assumes μ̂_{i|i-1} = μ̂_{i-1} contradicting the non-stationary distribution motivation; Eq. 9 uses current batch to approximate population variance, potentially circular
Limited experimental scope: Only continuous control tasks (MuJoCo), shallow networks (2 layers, 256 neurons), fixed time step of 5; scalability and generalization unclear

Missing hyperparameter sensitivity: No ablation or analysis for momentum α, re-calibration interval T_cal, batch count M, or batch size N despite their critical importance; no investigation of domain-specific tuning
Energy efficiency unvalidated: Energy benefits claimed but never experimentally verified; all evaluations on standard hardware with no neuromorphic hardware deployment
Re-BN implementation ambiguity: Unclear details on batch sampling strategy, early-stage replay buffer handling, and initialization of D^μ_i and D^σ_i
Limited novelty: Confidence-weighted averaging (Kalman filtering) and batch aggregation are standard techniques; primary contribution is domain-specific combination rather than novel algorithms

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear demonstration of the BN breakdown in online RL through effective visualization (Figure 1)
Principled theoretical approach: Theorem 1 derives confidence-guided weights from optimal linear estimation theory with Kalman filtering intuition
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple neuron models (LIF, CLIF, DN), RL algorithms (DQN, DDPG, TD3, SAC), and domains (Atari, MuJoCo)
Consistent and practical improvements: up to 22.6% gains over vanilla SNNs with no inference overhead due to weight fusion
Thorough empirical validation with proper baselines, ablations, and comparisons against other BN variants (tdBN, BNTT, TEBN, TABN)
Strong practical result: SNNs with CaRe-BN outperform ANNs by 5.9%, valuable for neuromorphic computing deployment
Good reproducibility: code availability, detailed hyperparameters in appendix, clear algorithmic descriptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: confidence-adaptive mechanism is essentially a Kalman-like filter applied to batch statistics; re-calibration is straightforward replay buffer resampling. Core ideas are incremental applications of existing techniques to a new domain

Incomplete theoretical analysis: (1) unbiasedness of Ca-BN estimator not formally proven despite relying on noisy confidence terms, (2) Gaussian assumption (Assumption 1) questionable for sparse spiking activations without empirical validation, (3) no convergence analysis or sample complexity bounds, (4) squared error proxies in Eq. 11 introduce unanalyzed bias

Overstated experimental claims: (1) 5.9% ANN outperformance is average across tasks with mixed individual results; (2) improvement over TABN is only ~2.65% despite claiming SOTA; (3) no formal significance testing; some improvements fall within error margins

Insufficient ablation and sensitivity analysis: recalibration frequency Tre=5000 appears arbitrary with no ablation; no sensitivity to recalibration batch count M=100 or momentum α=0.8; Figure 6(c) shows individual components help but combination analysis is shallow

Questionable design choices: no regularization for potentially pathological confidence weights (Eqs. 5-6); squared error variance proxies vs. alternatives unjustified; compounding approximation errors from Eq. 9 and Eq. 11 not characterized

Limited experimental scope: small networks (256 hidden units) without evaluation on larger architectures; standard benchmark environments only; only 5 random seeds in most experiments (modern standard is 10+)

ANN results suggest narrow contribution: Figure 6(d) shows ~0% improvement for ANNs, raising the question whether improvements are primarily from SNNs' dependence on normalization rather than CaRe-BN's innovation

Missing comparisons and analysis: no engagement with online normalization techniques from broader literature; limited comparison with LayerNorm/InstanceNorm variants; no explanation for why existing online BN methods fail; incomplete energy analysis (only inference, not training overhead)

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates why SNNs critically need BN while ANNs don't, and why traditional BN fails in online RL due to non-stationary distributions
Principled theoretical approach: Theorem 1 provides elegant Kalman filter-inspired derivation for optimal confidence-weighted statistics estimation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive evaluation across Atari and MuJoCo environments, multiple RL algorithms (DQN, DDPG, TD3, SAC), multiple neuron models (LIF, CLIF, DN), with proper ablations and 5 random seeds
Strong and consistent empirical results: Improvements up to 22.6%, SNNs outperform ANNs by 5.9%, reduced variance, quantitative evidence of improved statistics via Wasserstein distance
Practical method with minimal overhead: No inference overhead (fuses into weights), negligible training cost (~2%), energy efficiency preserved (107× reduction vs ANNs), easy drop-in replacement
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-written with effective visualizations, extensive hyperparameter details in appendix, strong experimental methodology
weaknesses: Limited theoretical rigor: Approximation in Eq. 10-11 using single-minibatch estimates as noisy probes lacks rigorous justification; no convergence analysis or error bounds; Gaussianity assumption may not hold for sparse spiking activations

Insufficient justification of design choices: Selection of hyperparameters (α=0.8, T_cal=5000, M=100) appears arbitrary with no ablation studies or sensitivity analysis; unclear why periodic re-calibration is necessary if Ca-BN is theoretically optimal

Limited mechanistic analysis: While Figure 3 shows improved statistics, the causal chain to policy improvement is empirically shown but theoretically unjustified; no analysis of failure modes or environments where method underperforms; missing discussion of how architecture/depth affects results

Incomplete baseline comparisons: SNN BN variants (tdBN, BNTT) designed for supervised learning, not RL; no comparison with domain adaptation or continual learning methods; ANN-SNN conversion baseline poorly justified
Neutral ANN results: CaRe-BN provides no benefit to ANNs, weakening evidence that improvements are truly SNN-specific rather than general RL regularization
Limited scope: Method specific to SNN-RL, a niche area with limited adoption in broader RL community; unclear how findings generalize beyond this setting
Missing sensitivity analysis: No ablations on critical hyperparameters (α, T_cal, M); no study of recalibration schedule sensitivity; only one configuration tested
Statistical concerns: No formal statistical significance tests reported; some improvements have overlapping confidence intervals; 5.9% improvement has non-trivial standard deviations
